notes.meaning: Paul introduces himself as an apostle sent by Jesus Christ, holding his office by the will of God rather than human choice. He addresses the believers in Ephesus as saints, which describes people set apart for God through trusting in Jesus. His greeting reminds Christians that their identity and purpose come directly from God.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars note that the words 'in Ephesus' are missing in the earliest manuscripts, indicating this may have been a circular letter sent to multiple churches across Asia Minor.

notes.meaning: Paul greets his readers with words of grace and peace. Grace is God's free, unearned favor, which always comes before a person can experience true peace with God. Both blessings flow equally from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

Paul praises God the Father for giving believers every spiritual blessing through their union with Jesus Christ. These gifts belong to the heavenly realm and are far greater and more lasting than any earthly riches. They assure Christians that God has already provided everything necessary for their spiritual life.

God chose believers in Christ before the foundation of the world was laid. His purpose in choosing them was that they should live holy lives, completely dedicated to Him and blameless in His sight. Holiness in heart and action is the true fruit of belonging to Jesus.

differ.view: God unconditionally chose specific individuals for salvation out of His sovereign mercy before creation.
God's eternal election rested on His foreknowledge of which individuals would freely believe in Christ.

notes.meaning: In love, God decided beforehand to adopt believers as His own sons and daughters through Jesus Christ. In ancient adoption, a child received full family rights and had all former debts canceled. God carried out this loving adoption simply because it pleased Him and matched the good pleasure of His will.

God planned this salvation so that people would praise His glorious grace, which is His wonderful, unearned favor. He freely poured out this grace on believers because they are united to His beloved Son. Because believers are accepted in Jesus, they can live with complete confidence in God's love.

In Christ, believers receive redemption through His blood, meaning they are bought out of slavery to sin by the price of His death on the cross. This sacrifice brings complete forgiveness for all our sins. It reveals the immense riches of God's grace, which offers freely what sinners could never earn.

God did not hold back His grace, but poured it out generously on His people. He did this with complete wisdom and understanding, designing a salvation that upholds His justice while rescuing sinners. This shows believers that God's mercy is guided by His perfect understanding.

God has now revealed the secret plan of His will that was hidden for many generations. This rescue plan came entirely from His own good pleasure and purpose in Christ. Believers can now understand the wonderful intention God kept in mind from the beginning.

When the appointed time fully arrives, God will gather all things together under Jesus Christ as the single Head. Sin brought disorder and rebellion into the world, but Christ brings everything in heaven and on earth back into perfect harmony. Believers can look forward to the day when the whole universe is united under His reign.

Believers have received an eternal inheritance in Christ because God predestined them according to His purpose. God is the ruler of all things, guiding every event according to His wise plan. Christians can trust that their future is safely secured in His hands.

Paul explains that those who were the first to hope in Christ, particularly early Jewish believers, were chosen to live for the praise of God's glory. Their salvation served to showcase God's power and faithfulness to the world. Every believer's life is meant to bring honor to the majesty of God.

Gentile believers also entered into this salvation when they heard the true gospel and believed in Jesus. When they put their faith in Him, God marked them as His own possession by giving them the promised Holy Spirit, much like a seal proves ownership on a document. This seal gives Christians deep assurance that they truly belong to God.

differ.view: Every believer is sealed permanently by the Holy Spirit at the moment of saving faith.
The sealing of the Spirit is often an experience of full assurance and inward holiness received some time after initial faith.

notes.meaning: The Holy Spirit in our hearts acts as a down payment or guarantee of the full inheritance God has in store for us. He remains with believers until the final day of redemption, when God completely frees His people from all sin, physical decay, and death. This complete rescue results in eternal praise to His glory.

Paul explains that ever since he heard reports of their steady faith in the Lord Jesus and their love for all God's people, he has not stopped giving thanks for them. He regularly mentions them before God in his prayers. True faith in Jesus always shows itself in active love for fellow Christians.

Paul asks God, the glorious Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, to grant believers a spirit of wisdom and revelation. He prays that the Holy Spirit will open their minds to understand divine truth and know God more intimately. Growing in the personal knowledge of God is the highest goal for every believer.

Paul prays that the eyes of their hearts will be filled with light so they can clearly see spiritual realities. He wants them to understand the confident hope God called them into, and to realize how rich and magnificent is the inheritance He shares with His people. Knowing these heavenly promises gives believers strength through daily trials.

Paul asks that believers recognize the exceeding greatness of God's power at work within those who believe. This is the very same mighty power God put on display when He raised Jesus from the dead and seated Him at His right hand in heaven. That same resurrection power works in believers today to give them spiritual life.

God exalted Jesus far above all earthly rulers, demonic forces, angelic powers, and every title of authority. His supreme rule stands unchallenged in this present world and will remain supreme for all eternity. Believers can rest safely knowing that no force in the universe is higher than their Savior.

God placed all things under the feet of Jesus and appointed Him to be the Head over everything for the benefit of the church. The church is Christ's spiritual body, joined closely to Him and receiving all its life and strength from Him. While Christ fills the entire universe with His presence and authority, He uniquely fills His church with His grace.
